summary.goal: OpenSEO is presented as an open source alternative to Semrush and Ahrefs, an SEO tool meant to give users keyword research, rank tracking, competitor insights, backlink data, site audits, and AI visibility tracking without the cost of established commercial suites.
summary.usage: OpenSEO can be tried for free on the hosted version at https://openseo.so, with an optional $10/month subscription to support the project. Alternatively, it can be self-hosted via Docker for personal, single-machine use, or via Cloudflare for internet-facing use across multiple devices or teams (works on the free plan); either self-hosting path requires a DataForSEO API key. Contributors can add a related skill with `npx skills add every-app/open-seo --skill simple-issue-description`.
summary.pros: The README states OpenSEO offers MCP and AI Skills integration for agents such as Claude Code, OpenClaw, and Hermes, a simple UI with focused SEO workflows instead of a bloated suite, no subscription requirement when self-hosting (only pay for DataForSEO usage), and the ability to fork and customize the tool.
summary.cons: Self-hosting via Docker is recommended only for personal, single-machine testing rather than team or multi-device use, and support for Railway, Coolify, or Dokploy is not yet as simple, with the project stating this is planned for future improvement. The hosted subscription is priced by charging 28% extra on top of underlying DataForSEO costs.
summary.fit: OpenSEO appears best suited for individuals or teams who want a self-controlled, pay-as-you-go SEO tool that integrates directly with AI agents, rather than users who prefer a fully managed subscription service with no self-hosting involved.

repos.name: K-Dense-AI / scientific-agent-skills
repos.description: Turn any AI agent into an AI Scientist. The #1 Agent Skills library for science, used by 190,000+ scientists worldwide. 165 ready-to-use validated skills plus 100+ scientific databases covering biology, chemistry, medicine, and drug discovery. Compatible with Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Antigravity, and the open Agent Skills standard.

summary.goal: Scientific Agent Skills is an open-source collection of 166 ready-to-use scientific and research skills for AI agents that support the Agent Skills standard. Created by K-Dense, it covers domains such as bioinformatics, cheminformatics, clinical research, and materials science.
summary.usage: Install with `npx skills add K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills` for supported hosts, or `gh skill install K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills` via the GitHub CLI; the repository also loads as an Agent Plugins package. It works with hosts including Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, and Google Antigravity, and requires Python 3.13+ with the uv package manager for repository tooling.
summary.pros: Each skill ships documentation, code examples, and best practices, plus a test suite for any skill that includes scripts. A unified database-lookup skill gives access to 78 public databases, and GitHub CLI installs support version pinning to a release tag or commit SHA for reproducibility.
summary.cons: Skills can execute code, install packages, and make network requests, so users are expected to review a skill's SKILL.md before installing rather than trust it automatically. Because 166 skills represent a large amount of standing context, the documentation suggests installing only a topical subset rather than the full collection.
summary.fit: This appears best suited for researchers or engineers who want to extend a compatible AI coding agent with domain-specific scientific workflows rather than build integrations from scratch. The repository is MIT licensed, but individual skills may carry separate licenses that should be checked before commercial use.

repos.name: melgarafael / DeskcommCRM
repos.description: Open-source AI sales OS — self-hosted CRM with native AI agents + WhatsApp (WAHA). Open alternative to Kommo, Octadesk & Intercom for any business that sells by chat. MCP-ready, multi-tenant, LGPD.
